name: s05_differentiation
description: Multicellularity S05 (differentiation). A fixed 5x5 patch of germ cells consumes O2 that diffuses in from the medium; interior cells go hypoxic, their stemness ODE decays and they differentiate to soma (type 2), which draws less O2. Germ cells grow only where local O2 is above a threshold. Emits fate_counts and viable_biomass. TRANSIENT/quasi-stable gradient: the O2 profile relaxes during the first updates; readouts are taken at the pinned window.

random_fraction.description: random arm: fraction of cells seeded as soma

grow_rate.description: germ target-volume growth per update where O2 >= threshold

cpm.doc:
process-bigraph wrapper around the Rust CPM engine, with a per-cell
coupling surface so subcellular processes can read the local environment
and drive differentiation via a cell-type switch.

_contract.summary: Advances a Cellular Potts (Glazier–Graner–Hogeweg) model by running `mcs_per_update` Monte Carlo sweeps of the wrapped Rust engine each process step. Each sweep attempts random boundary copies between adjacent lattice sites and accepts or rejects them by the Metropolis rule on the change ΔH in a Hamiltonian that sums cell–cell adhesion, a per-cell volume constraint, and a per-cell surface-area constraint (plus any optional terms the spec opts in). Before stepping it applies incoming cell-type switches (`fates`), and after stepping it emits per-cell geometry (volumes, types, centre-of-mass positions) and local-environment readouts (mean field value at each cell, count of secretory neighbours) so subcellular processes can couple to the tissue.
_contract.description:
Core cellular-dynamics engine of the workspace. The morphology lives in a Rust `World` built from a declarative CPM `spec` (see viva_cpm.schema.load_world); this Process owns the step loop and the coupling surface to process-bigraph.

Energy terms compose additively in the Metropolis Hamiltonian; each term's `*_type` list opts specific cell types in, so tissues mix behaviours. The core terms are:
  - Adhesion/contact: sum over neighbouring site pairs of different cells of the contact energy J(tau_a, tau_b) between their types (the `contact` adhesion matrix).
  - Volume constraint: lambda_V * (V - V_target)^2 per cell.
  - Surface constraint: lambda_S * (S - S_target)^2 per cell.
Optional spec terms (chemotaxis on reaction-diffusion fields, connectivity, basement membrane, junctions, elongation length, external force) add further contributions to ΔH but are not computed in this wrapper.

Each update: (1) write incoming fates into the engine as cell-type switches; (2) run `mcs_per_update` Monte Carlo sweeps (each sweep also advances the reaction-diffusion fields when present); (3) read back per-cell geometry and the per-cell environment readouts used for subcellular coupling.

Two optional config knobs, both no-ops when unset: `mitosis` (after each sweep block, grow and then divide the listed cell types to drive growth-driven proliferation) and `report_aggregate_types` (the cell types merged into one mask for the propagule metrics n_propagules and largest_cluster_fraction).

inputs.fates: map[integer] keyed by string cell id -> new cell-type tag. Lets a subcellular process drive differentiation by wiring a single cell's fate at `[fates, str(cid)]`; each non-zero value for a positive cell id is applied via world.set_cell_type before the sweeps. The composite pre-seeds a key per wired cell so per-key overwrites land (an absent map key would be dropped).

outputs.volumes: overwrite[list] of current cell volumes V (lattice-site counts), indexed by cell id (index 0 is the medium); emitted as a whole list each step.
outputs.types: overwrite[list] of each cell's current type tag tau, indexed by cell id (index 0 is the medium).
outputs.positions: overwrite[list] of each cell's centre-of-mass [x, y, z] in lattice units, indexed by cell id.
outputs.field_at_cell: overwrite[map[float]] keyed by string cell id -> mean value of field 0 over the cell's occupied sites (empty when n_fields == 0). The overwrite wrapper replaces the whole store atomically so a subcell can read `[field_at_cell, str(cid)]`.
outputs.neighbor_secretory: overwrite[map[integer]] keyed by string cell id -> number of distinct face-adjacent neighbour cells whose type is in `secretory_types` (medium and same-cell contacts excluded).
outputs.n_propagules: overwrite[integer] number of connected components of the aggregated `report_aggregate_types` mask, i.e. how many detached propagules the clonal cluster has fragmented into; emitted only when `report_aggregate_types` is set.
outputs.largest_cluster_fraction: overwrite[float] the largest connected component's share of the masked sites (1.0 = fully cohesive); emitted only when `report_aggregate_types` is set.
outputs.fate_counts: overwrite[map[integer]] keyed by string cell-type tag -> number of non-medium cells of that type; emitted only when `report_fate_growth` is true.
outputs.viable_biomass: overwrite[float] total volume (lattice sites) of non-medium cells with volume >= 1; emitted only when `report_fate_growth` is true.

config.spec: Declarative CPM tree passed to load_world: potts block (dims, boundary, neighbor_order, temperature T, seed), cell/seed-label placement with per-cell target_volume/lambda_volume/target_surface/lambda_surface, the contact adhesion matrix J, optional reaction-diffusion fields, and optional extension terms.
config.mcs_per_update: integer (default 10): number of Monte Carlo sweeps (MCS) the engine runs per process update — the number of simulated CPM time units advanced each step.
config.n_fields: integer (default 0): number of reaction-diffusion fields; when > 0 the mean of field 0 at each cell is emitted on field_at_cell.
config.secretory_types: list (default []) of cell-type tags treated as secretory when tallying neighbor_secretory face-adjacency counts.
config.mitosis: optional list (default [], no-op when empty) of {type, grow_rate, divide_threshold, reset_target}: after each step, grow every cell of `type` by `grow_rate` target volume, then divide cells with volume >= `divide_threshold`, resetting their target volume to `reset_target`. An entry may carry `o2_gate` = {field, threshold}: then each cell of `type` grows by `grow_rate` only if its mean local field value >= threshold, and division is skipped unless both `divide_threshold` and `reset_target` are given.
config.report_fate_growth: boolean (default false): when true, fate_counts and viable_biomass are emitted.
config.report_aggregate_types: optional list (default [], no-op when empty) of cell-type tags aggregated into one mask; when set, n_propagules and largest_cluster_fraction are emitted.

math: 1\ \text{MCS} = N\ \text{copy attempts},\quad N = \text{number of lattice sites}

symbols.sigma: cell index (spin) labelling the cell occupying a lattice site (dimensionless; 0 = medium)
symbols.tau_sigma: cell-type tag of cell sigma, selecting adhesion and constraint parameters (dimensionless)
symbols.J: contact (adhesion) energy between two abutting cell types from the contact matrix (energy units)
symbols.H: total CPM Hamiltonian, sum of adhesion, volume, and surface energies (energy units)
symbols.\u0394H: change in H produced by a single trial site-copy, used in the Metropolis rule (energy units)
symbols.V_sigma: current volume of cell sigma (number of lattice sites, voxels)
symbols.V_target: target volume V* of a cell set by its type (voxels)
symbols.lambda_V: volume-constraint stiffness, penalty per squared volume deviation (energy / voxel^2)
symbols.S_sigma: current surface area of cell sigma (number of boundary faces, sites)
symbols.S_target: target surface area S* of a cell set by its type (sites)
symbols.lambda_S: surface-constraint stiffness, penalty per squared surface deviation (energy / site^2)
symbols.T: CPM temperature / fluctuation amplitude in the Metropolis acceptance exp(-ΔH/T) (energy units)
symbols.MCS: Monte Carlo sweep: N site-copy attempts where N is the number of lattice sites (time unit)
symbols.mcs_per_update: Monte Carlo sweeps advanced per process step (sweeps)

assumptions: Dynamics (Hamiltonian evaluation, trial copies, Metropolis acceptance, field PDE integration) live in the wrapped Rust engine; this Process only drives the step loop and the port coupling.
Energy terms are additive and each term's `*_type` list opts specific cell types in, so only the core adhesion/volume/surface terms are always present.
Cell ids are contiguous positive integers with 0 reserved for the medium; per-cell output lists are indexed by id and the id-0 medium slot is excluded from the per-cell maps.
fates are applied as hard type switches before stepping; a value of 0 or a non-positive cell id is ignored.
neighbor_secretory counts only face-adjacent (6-neighbour) distinct cell pairs; medium and same-cell contacts do not count.
field_at_cell reports only field index 0 and is empty unless n_fields > 0.
references: Graner & Glazier (1992), Simulation of biological cell sorting using a two-dimensional extended Potts model, Phys. Rev. Lett. 69:2013.
Glazier & Graner (1993), Simulation of the differential adhesion driven rearrangement of biological cells, Phys. Rev. E 47:2128.
Hogeweg (2000), Evolving mechanisms of morphogenesis: on the interplay between differential adhesion and cell differentiation, J. Theor. Biol. 203:317.

sbml_1.doc:
Per-cell SBML ODE via viva-tellurium. The environmental ligand is pushed
into a held floating species each step; a chosen species is published as
the cell's scalar ``state`` (e.g. stemness).

_contract.description: type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type

bool_1.doc:
A minimal synchronous Boolean fate switch with Notch-style lateral
inhibition. When stemness falls below threshold the cell differentiates:
it becomes secretory (goblet) unless a neighbour already committed
secretory, in which case it becomes absorptive. Deterministic.

_contract.description: type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type

emitter.doc:
Append simulation state to a SQLite database each timestep.

One row per step, with the full state tree stored as JSON. The database
file is a single ``.db`` file that can be opened with any SQLite client,
queried with SQL, and kept for long-term storage. Multiple simulations
can share one file — rows are partitioned by ``simulation_id``.

To record the composite config or other metadata alongside the history
rows, call :func:`save_simulation_metadata` after constructing the
Composite — the emitter itself only writes the per-step history rows.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 = every
tick). The ``step`` column still stores the true composite tick number,
so time-series produced from the history reflect the real cadence even
though intermediate ticks were not persisted. Use this when a Composite
fires the emitter very often (small intervals, long runs) and you don't
need every tick in the archive — it's the cheapest way to shrink the
write volume without losing the simulation's time axis.

``batch_size`` buffers up to N recorded rows in memory and flushes them
in a single SQL transaction (default 1 = write each row immediately).
With ``batch_size=100`` the per-row fsync overhead is amortized across
the batch, giving a large speedup on high-frequency runs. Unflushed
rows are guaranteed to be written on ``close()`` and on the next
``query()``; a hard crash before flush loses the buffered rows.

_contract.description: type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type
